title: Secure the client/server boundary
summary: Treat every remote call as an untrusted request. The server decides what the player is allowed to do.
do: Validate types, bounds, permissions and rate limits before work.
Compute rewards and damage from server-owned state.
avoid: Do not accept a client-supplied currency balance.
Do not treat a UI cooldown as a security boundary.

title: Keep authority and secrets on the server
summary: Separate shared presentation from privileged game rules and credentials.
do: Keep server-only modules in server containers.
Review what replicates to players.
avoid: Do not place secrets in replicated modules.
Do not trust obfuscated client code to protect valuable logic.

title: Design systems that resist abuse
summary: Prevent impossible actions by designing narrow server APIs and explicit invariants.
do: Define legal transitions before implementing remotes.
Test repeated and out-of-order requests.
avoid: Do not add trust checks only after an exploit report.
Do not let one request perform unbounded work.

title: Audit third-party assets and scripts
summary: Treat imported models and packages as code dependencies that need inspection.
do: Inspect scripts and dependencies before insertion.
Keep a saved place version before major imports.
avoid: Do not run unknown loader scripts blindly.
Do not assume a popular asset is automatically safe.

title: Build reliable player data storage
summary: Plan records, concurrent updates, retries and recovery before shipping progression.
do: Keep related persistent values together when they must change atomically.
Handle failed requests explicitly and observe failures.
avoid: Do not overwrite a failed load with a fresh default profile.
Do not assume every storage operation succeeds.

title: Handle storage errors and budgets
summary: Read current limits and error meanings when designing persistence.
do: Use bounded retry policies and watch request budgets.
Exercise failure handling in a separate test environment.
avoid: Do not retry forever in a tight loop.
Do not copy numeric limits into a design without checking the source.

title: Understand data versions and caching
summary: Use documented version and cache behavior to plan recovery and consistency.
do: Document which reads may be cached.
Plan and rehearse recovery from a bad data release.
avoid: Do not assume a repeated read always reaches the backend.
Do not treat application-level undo as a complete backup.

title: Choose remote events and callbacks
summary: Choose communication patterns based on whether a response is required.
do: Keep message payloads small and well defined.
Validate requests at the receiving boundary.
avoid: Do not block unrelated work waiting on unnecessary callbacks.
Do not send whole instance hierarchies when identifiers will do.

title: Prefer event-driven systems
summary: React to meaningful changes instead of continuously polling everything.
do: Disconnect event connections when their owner is destroyed.
Keep event handlers focused and bounded.
avoid: Do not accumulate duplicate listeners after respawns.
Do not scan the entire world every frame.

title: Build worlds that support streaming
summary: Design clients to handle instances arriving and leaving as the world streams.
do: Handle missing and streamed-out instances.
Test travel and respawn across distant areas.
avoid: Do not assume every workspace descendant exists on each client.
Do not force the whole map to remain loaded by default.

title: Use streaming techniques deliberately
summary: Choose model behavior and loading strategies around actual gameplay needs.
do: Group meaningful world units and test their behavior.
Use focused loading strategies for critical interactions.
avoid: Do not apply persistence settings to every model.
Do not hide loading problems only on a powerful desktop.

title: Design robust NPC navigation
summary: Navigation needs replanning, failure handling and a world built for traversable routes.
do: Handle blocked paths and unavailable routes.
Test stairs, obstacles and moving targets.
avoid: Do not recompute every NPC path every frame.
Do not assume a computed route can never become blocked.

title: Design for constrained devices
summary: Set a baseline device and measure memory, scene complexity and script cost early.
do: Reuse assets and keep replicated content intentional.
Prefer event-driven work and clean up connections.
avoid: Do not put all game assets in ReplicatedStorage.
Do not optimize only for a development workstation.

title: Identify the real performance bottleneck
summary: Measure the slow subsystem before changing code or art.
do: Capture measurements in a repeatable scenario.
Separate CPU, rendering, network and memory symptoms.
avoid: Do not use guesswork as evidence of an optimization.
Do not compare two different scenes as a benchmark.

title: Improve frame rate and loading
summary: Use the measured bottleneck to choose targeted improvements.
do: Keep initial content lean and defer optional work.
Measure before and after each significant change.
avoid: Do not preload the entire game as a default.
Do not replicate cosmetic work that can stay local.

title: Read the MicroProfiler
summary: Use frame timing evidence to understand stalls and expensive work.
do: Profile representative play sessions.
Investigate spikes as well as averages.
avoid: Do not conclude performance is good from average FPS alone.
Do not leave heavy debug instrumentation enabled unnecessarily.

title: Test multiplayer behavior in Studio
summary: Use the appropriate Studio test mode and inspect both client and server behavior.
do: Run multi-client tests for shared-state features.
Check output, respawn and disconnect scenarios.
avoid: Do not declare multiplayer ready after a single solo run.
Do not use an implementation summary as test evidence.

title: Make the game accessible
summary: Make interactions understandable and usable across different player needs.
do: Provide readable text, clear feedback and redundant cues.
Review contrast and avoid relying on color alone.
avoid: Do not make essential information available only through audio.
Do not use motion or visual noise that obscures gameplay.

title: Make UI adapt to different screens
summary: Combine layout constraints and scaling so interfaces remain usable on real devices.
do: Check narrow screens and large text.
Use consistent layout rules instead of positioning each element independently.
avoid: Do not assume a fixed desktop resolution.
Do not shrink every label until it fits.

title: Design useful mobile controls
summary: Treat touch input as a primary interaction model with its own constraints.
do: Test touch targets on devices and avoid control overlap.
Consider orientation and screen-safe areas.
avoid: Do not rely on hover for essential actions.
Do not crowd the movement and camera control areas.

title: Support controller navigation
summary: Make focus, selection and feedback clear for players using controllers.
do: Provide visible focus and predictable navigation.
Test prompts and menus with a controller.
avoid: Do not require a mouse to dismiss a mandatory dialog.
Do not lose focus when panels change.

title: Build a satisfying core loop
summary: Identify the repeated action, feedback and motivation that carry the experience.
do: Prototype the central action early.
Make the result of an action legible and rewarding.
avoid: Do not add many systems before the main interaction works.
Do not confuse a list of features with a playable loop.

title: Help players understand the first session
summary: Teach the minimum needed to reach meaningful play and a clear next goal.
do: Observe where new players become confused.
Introduce mechanics when players can use them.
avoid: Do not front-load every rule in a wall of text.
Do not make players wait through a long introduction before acting.

title: Teach through interaction
summary: Choose teaching techniques that support the experience and the player’s immediate goal.
do: Use timely feedback and simple early tasks.
Test with someone who has never seen the game.
avoid: Do not assume the developer’s knowledge is obvious to newcomers.
Do not block progress with unclear instructions.

title: Balance sources, sinks and progression
summary: Model how value enters and leaves the economy across new and experienced players.
do: Track currency sources and sinks.
Test progression under multiple player behaviors.
avoid: Do not tune rewards from one idealized playthrough.
Do not inflate rewards without considering long-term accumulation.

title: Design monetization around player value
summary: Plan purchases as part of a coherent experience and review current platform requirements.
do: Make offers understandable and relevant.
Evaluate how purchases affect game balance.
avoid: Do not obscure what a player is buying.
Do not assume every game benefits from the same monetization pattern.

title: Implement repeatable purchases correctly
summary: Separate purchase prompts from durable server-side fulfillment.
do: Follow the current receipt-processing contract.
Make fulfillment resilient to repeated delivery and failures.
avoid: Do not grant items just because a purchase prompt closed.
Do not treat the client as the payment authority.

title: Measure the in-game economy
summary: Use economy instrumentation to investigate value flow and player progression.
do: Give events consistent names and useful context.
Compare player segments and progression stages.
avoid: Do not collect events without a question they can answer.
Do not infer an entire economy from a global average.

title: Understand retention without guessing
summary: Use cohorts and repeat behavior to evaluate whether players return.
do: Compare cohorts after a specific product change.
Pair metrics with observed player experience.
avoid: Do not confuse acquisition spikes with retention improvements.
Do not infer causation from one noisy day.

title: Plan sustainable content updates
summary: Treat updates as a repeatable production and learning cycle.
do: Scope changes around player value and delivery capacity.
Plan QA and monitoring before release.
avoid: Do not ship unrelated risky changes as one untraceable bundle.
Do not expand the live scope faster than the team can maintain.

title: Operate and improve a live game
summary: Plan ongoing operation around evidence, reliable updates and player expectations.
do: Set a sustainable cadence and watch player feedback.
Prepare operational checklists for time-sensitive events.
avoid: Do not make every update depend on a last-minute manual step.
Do not judge success only by launch-day attention.
